To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we isolated 7 bacterial genera with coaggregation abilities from 8 different aquatic environments, and we found that Bacillus megaterum T1 and B. cereus G5 had broad-spectrum co-aggregation abilities.

a novel bridging bacteria, Bacillus cereusG5, has been isolated from the water environment, and it has a broad-spectrum aggregation ability and could mediate the integrationof exogenous degrading bacterial strains into biofilms.

we isolated and identified a broad spectrum coagingating bacteria from water environments and evaluated the coagingating ability of 22 strains with 21 other strains, and we found two strains with broad spectrum coaggregation property.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of broad-spectrum coaggregateing bacteria, which could be applied in bioaugmentation.
the isolation of coaggregating bacteria from natural water systems, the identification of their coaggregating partners and the characterization of their biofilm development.
the isolation of broad spectrum coaggregation bacteria from different water environments, which may be useful to bioaugmentation treatment of contaminated water systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coaggregation property of G5 and the coexistence of it with other strains in the biofilms are the key factors for its broad-spectrum coaugmenting ability.
the broad spectrum coaggregation property of bridging bacteria, like G5, is an important factor for biofilm formation and bioaugmentation.
G5 and Tl are bridging bacteria with a broad spectrum of coaggregation property, and G5 could mediate bioaugmentation of 3,5-Dinitrobenzoate-degrading strain A3.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we successfully isolated a broad spectrum coaggregateing bacteria from different water systems for potential use in bioaugmentation treatment.
the bridging bacteria with a broad spectrum of coaggregating property could be used as a tool for bioaugmentation.
we have successfully isolated and characterized a broad spectrum bridging bacteria, G5, which has a great potential for use in the bioaugmentation of water treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the coaggregation of bacteria can be easily and rapidly screened by a visual and semi quantitative assay, and the broad spectrum coaggregation bacteria can be isolated and identified from water environments.

the bridging bacteria with a broad spectrum of coaggregation ability, such as B. cereus G5, could mediate the integration and development of exogenous degradable strains into biofilms, which could be a potential strategy for the bioaugmentation of bioremediation of contaminated water environments.

bridging bacteria with a broad spectrum of coaggregation can facilitate the integration of exogenously introduced degrading bacteria in the biofilms, and thus contribute to the biofilm-based bioaugmentation treatment.
